column1: # Questions for the TOOLS half of `recall.py --exam`: "is there a command or MCP tool that does this?"
# question <TAB> the command(s) or MCP tool(s) that answer it (any of, |), or `none` when the right answer is that nothing here does.
# Where the questions come from. A question a tool's author writes after reading the tool's description is a
# question the description already answers. So these are sentences that were written BEFORE this file, by
# someone who needed the thing and did not find it here: the first sentence of the docstring of a tool a work
# wrote for itself (roms/261011_edo/tools, roms/260816_transistor/tools), copied verbatim on 2026-10-13, and
# three questions typed into recall.py that day while checking those tools against this repository. The
# expected answers are from the works' own reviews (which command came nearest); `none` is a correct answer.
# Frozen before any command was given an "Answers:" line. Add questions; do not reword one to make it pass.
# Changed since, and why: 2026-10-13, `cmd/sound` was written because two works had each built a tool for it. The
# key of "Dump a ROM's TIA audio registers ..." gained `sound` (the question's words are untouched; the command
# writes them as text, not JSON), and the last question was added -- the first sentence of the header of
# roms/261011_edo/tools/sound/main.go, verbatim, written two days before the command.
Picture of the current ROM against the original's, zone by zone, aligned at zone bottoms.
Does a build show the same scenes, in the same order, moving the same way, as the original?
Re-record the pins of scenarios/fire-held.json from the current ROM.
Run a source under each of the fourteen shipped settings (tools/settings.py) and count what the frame loop does
How good is the scene generator's randomness?
Render one frame of a ROM with controller actions HELD, as a PNG.
Dump a ROM's TIA audio registers, one frame at a time, as JSON.
Render a ROM to the pictures Shinji can actually look at, and `open` them.
Which key and which voices make this figure LOW and DARK, not bright.
What does the TIA's NOISE actually put in each frequency band?
compare the RAM of two ROMs frame by frame to show a rewrite did not change behaviour
press the fire button at random times and see whether a frame is ever not 262 lines
is the picture my build draws the same as the original ROM's, pixel by pixel
run a ROM on the Gopher2600 engine and write down what it plays.
